facts.statement: Navajoceratops is a genus of ceratopsid dinosaur that lived during the late Cretaceous Period in North America.
facts.quote: Navajoceratops (meaning "Navajo horned face") is a genus of ceratopsid dinosaur from the late Cretaceous Period of what is now North America.

facts.statement: Navajoceratops fossils were discovered in the Campanian Hunter Wash Member of the Kirtland Formation in New Mexico.
facts.quote: It was discovered in the Campanian Hunter Wash Member of the Kirtland Formation, New Mexico.

facts.statement: Navajoceratops is classified as a member of the subfamily Chasmosaurinae.
facts.quote: Navajoceratops was a member of the Chasmosaurinae.

facts.statement: Navajoceratops lived during the Campanian stage of the late Cretaceous, approximately 75 to 73 million years ago, in what is now North America.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Cretácico, durante el Campaniense, hace aproximadamente 75-73 millones de años en lo que ahora es Norteamérica.

facts.statement: Navajoceratops belongs to the family Ceratopsidae.
Navajoceratops belongs to the subfamily Chasmosaurinae.
The species name sullivani honors Robert M. Sullivan, the leader of the expeditions that recovered the partial skull holotype specimen in 2002.
facts.quote: Fue llamada así por Robert M. Sullivan, líder de las expediciones que recuperaron el espécimen holotipo, SMP VP-1500, recolectado en 2002, consiste en un cráneo parcial.

facts.statement: Navajoceratops lived between 83.6 and 72.2 million years ago during the Campanian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Campanian (83.6 to 72.2 million years ago)
